question: A cement laboratory compares 28-day compressive-strength results from two production lots, but one report calculates specimen age from casting and the other from demoulding; how should an agent establish comparable test ages before interpreting a strength change?
scenario: Inconsistent specimen-age origins in comparative 28-day strength reports
evidence_required: Original casting date and time, demoulding time and actual compression-test timestamp for each specimen
Applicable test method, specimen geometry, curing environment and batch/sample identification
Calibrated compression-machine records, replicate results and any deviations from prescribed test-age tolerance
answer_and_decision_guide: Reconstruct each specimen's elapsed age from the origin specified by the applicable test method; do not substitute demoulding time for casting time. Confirm curing and sampling comparability, identify specimens outside the relevant test-method tolerance and separate those deviations from genuine lot-to-lot strength differences. Do not declare compliance or adjust plant operation without method-specific laboratory review.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained contextual reference; exact test-standard edition, public live access and laboratory applicability require independent verification.
free_first_decision: First review the free article, original laboratory worksheets and applicable published test method; a paid package is unnecessary if these resolve the age-basis discrepancy.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Only consider an exact verified relevant file after checking edition, permission, price and explicit buyer authorization; never initiate payment.

model_limitations: Cannot inspect original specimen timestamps, calibrated machine records, licensed standards or actual curing conditions; cannot certify laboratory compliance.
